Author: Krishan Pahal

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:239038
Court No. - 72
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13747 of 2023
Applicant :- Situ
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pankaj Kumar Mishra

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vijay Kumar Pandey,Vineeta Devi
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

Heard Sri Aditya Verma, learned Advocate holding brief for Sri Pranshu Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Vijay Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Pranshu Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
2.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 104 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Phaphund, District Auraiya, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
3. As per prosecution story, the minor daughter of the informant is stated to have been found missing since 18.3.2023 at about 10.00 am when she had gone to the shop of the tailor.
Later on, it came to the knowledge of the informant that it was the applicant, who had enticed away the victim.

1

entities.text: Situ vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim is stated to have taken away cash worth Rs. 10,000/- and certain ornaments.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of his arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
Learned counsel has next stated that the FIR is delayed by about six days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The victim has not hurled any kind of allegations against the applicant in the statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C.
It is further stated that the victim has mentioned her age to be 20 years in her statement recorded therein by the Magistrate.

Learned counsel has next stated that as per school certificate,
the date of birth is 10.7.2005 that falls few months below 18 years.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant has placed much reliance on the settled case law of the Apex Court in Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673, wherein it has been stated that it is more often in the Indian Society that person shows the age of their wards much below than their actual age.
6.

entities.text: Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, he will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

7. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail on account of her age, but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

8. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgement of the Apex Court.
8. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

entities.text: Situ vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicant.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Justice Krishan Pahal) Order Date :- 18.12.2023 Shalini  Situ vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81226561/
